headline: High: Continue can write shared workspace files and use MCP, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks with Botpress’s LLM-driven support workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is an LLM chatbot and Continue can use MCP plus read/write workspace files, so a shared-file or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content influence Botpress prompts. The exact ingestion path is not documented, so I avoid high severity, but the interaction is plausible in default IDE/workspace setups.
conditions: IF Botpress reads content from files or MCP outputs as instructions
IF Continue is configured to expose workspace text to Botpress through a shared file or MCP server
mitigations: Disable shared-file handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on any MCP-fed content
Restrict Botpress to trusted system prompts only
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue explicitly reads workspace files and open editor buffers and can egress broadly; Botpress is a customer-support agent that may process user content. If both touch the same workspace or support artifacts, Continue can transmit sensitive file contents outward. Botpress’s own egress is none, so the leakage path is asymmetric but still real.
conditions: IF Botpress stores support transcripts or secrets in files that Continue can read
IF Continue is connected to a remote model provider or MCP server with broad egress
mitigations: Keep support data out of the shared workspace
Point Continue at a local-only model provider
Separate credentials and secrets from editor buffers
Disable MCP servers that can exfiltrate file contents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem and shared-state-via-filesystem concurrency, while Botpress can install packages. Even though Botpress lacks explicit filesystem write in the profile, the pair can still contend over shared files and generated artifacts in the same workspace, creating overwrite or race risks. Uncertainty about Botpress’s write surface keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF Botpress writes generated artifacts or package changes through its runtime environment
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize file writes with a lock file
Disable package installation in shared workspaces
Review generated diffs before saving
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent and Continue is a coding assistant that can act through MCP and shell/file tools. If Botpress output is treated as authoritative by Continue, or Continue’s generated code/config is fed back into Botpress workflows, mistakes can cascade into incorrect support actions or unsafe code changes. The pairwise action chain is plausible by default, so I rate it high.
conditions: IF Continue consumes Botpress-generated text without verification
IF Botpress forwards Continue-produced code or instructions into downstream actions
mitigations: Add a human review step before any action
Require source citations for Botpress-derived facts
Block automatic execution of Continue-generated shell commands
Limit Botpress outputs to summaries, not directives
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a support agent and Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and model-provider API keys. If support transcripts or regulated data are placed into the same workspace, Continue’s broad egress and external model-provider calls can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated support data is stored in files accessible to Continue
IF Continue sends those files to a non-compliant external model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of editor buffers
Use a compliant/local model provider
Separate support and code workspaces
Review retention settings for any connected provider
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
